IsUsedUp.rationale: LizardTail.cs:18 is `IsUsedUp => _wasUsed`; lizard_tail.py:31-33 is `return self._used`. Correct and load-bearing: Relic.is_tradable (relics/base.py:126-136) refuses a used-up relic, so a spent Lizard Tail stops being offerable to the trade events on both sides, and Rare rarity does not otherwise exclude it. The Status = RelicStatus.Disabled the C# setter also performs (LizardTail.cs:33-37) is presentation (N4). The LIFETIME is per-RUN, not per-combat, on both sides -- [SavedProperty] on WasUsed (LizardTail.cs:22) means it survives a save, and `self._used` is set in __init__ and never reset. `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py sweep-reset` lists lizard_tail among the never-reset candidates whose C# relic has NO combat-boundary reset, which is exactly the evidence that per-run is intended; the sim's own docstring (lizard_tail.py:15) says 'once per combat' and is WRONG, but the code is right. Note that means the port's docstring is the only thing to fix in this member. Rule 7: relics/base.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 8): `ShouldDieLate` is a pure predicate now, and the entry's stated blocker was itself stale. THE FIX: LizardTail.cs:40-51 reads `WasUsed` and returns -- `creature != Owner.Creature -> true`, `WasUsed -> true`, else false -- and the charge is spent in AfterPreventingDeath (:53-59, `Flash(); WasUsed = true;` then the heal). relics/lizard_tail.py set `_used` INSIDE the predicate, so a second query in the same breath answered the wrong way and any caller that queried without continuing to the prevention path burned the relic. `should_die_late` now only reads, `after_preventing_death` sets `_used`, and the `_heal_pending` shim is GONE -- `Hook.AfterPreventingDeath` is dispatched to the VETOING listener alone (CreatureCmd.cs:567; the sim's dispatcher walks the `preventer` list), so there was nothing to re-check. THE BLOCKER WAS STALE: the entry's FIX-ORDERING CONSTRAINT said this needed `DamageCmd.deal` to pass a preventer list on every path and that `CreatureCmd.kill` did not. It does -- `cmds._resolve_death` builds the list, passes it to `hooks.should_die` and calls `hooks.after_preventing_death(preventer, target)` on the else-arm, and `CreatureCmd.kill` routes through `_resolve_death`. And the entry's named LIVE witness was `cards/breakthrough.py`'s bare `if p.hp <= 0 and ctx.hooks.should_die(p)`, which ROUND 7 DELETED when card/breakthrough/OnPlay moved the self-damage into DamageCmd.deal. ENUMERATED 2026-07-29: `hooks.should_die(` has exactly ONE caller in sts2_rl (`_resolve_death`), and it always continues to the prevention path; the run-level walk (run.py) iterates the POTION BELT only, which is Fairy in a Bottle, not this relic. So the impurity was no longer observable at the moment it was fixed -- recorded here rather than used as an excuse to leave it, because the predicate now has the shape the source has. EXECUTED: three consecutive `should_die_late` queries all answer False and leave `is_used_up` False; a real lethal hit spends the charge, heals off 0 and leaves the player alive; a second lethal hit kills; another creature's death answers True and spends nothing. Every sim caller that queries should_die without going on to run the prevention path therefore consumes the relic for nothing. EXECUTED (b08-lizard): cards/breakthrough.py:49's `if p.hp <= 0 and ctx.hooks.should_die(p)` is exactly that shape -- the veto makes the `if` false, so breakthrough does nothing at all: no HP floor, no after_preventing_death, no on_damage_received -- and the player is left at hp=0 with _used=True. CreatureCmd.kill (cmds.py:192-207) is the second such caller. This is the SAME mechanism audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard G4 describes from the other side (the killing-blow AfterDamageReceived skip that the port relies on), and that record explicitly notes the port 'relies on this on_damage_received re-fire to perform its heal'. What it does not record, and this entry does, is that the reliance also puts the CHARGE in the wrong place. FIX-ORDERING CONSTRAINT: moving the heal to after_preventing_death (which exists, hooks.py:596-601) fixes G1, G2 and G3 together, but it also means DamageCmd.deal must pass a preventer list on every path -- CreatureCmd.kill currently does not. guards.what: N2: the heal ARITHMETIC -- `Math.Max(1m, (decimal)MaxHp * (HealVar(50).BaseValue / 100m))` (LizardTail.cs:57) vs `max(1, self.player.max_hp * self.HEAL_PCT // 100)` (lizard_tail.py:53)
guards.rationale: Verified rather than assumed, because a decimal-vs-integer rounding slip here would be invisible. No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so HealVar(50) is the pinned non-ascension value and BaseValue is the contract's read. C# keeps the half in decimal and truncates only when CurrentHp is assigned -- SetCurrentHpInternal is `CurrentHp = (int)Math.Min(amount, MaxHp)` -- and because CurrentHp is an integer, truncating `hp + 40.5` gives the same result as adding `floor(40.5)`. So `max_hp * 50 // 100` is the right integer form for every max HP, EXECUTED at 80, 81 and 1 (b08-lizard). The `Math.Max(1, ...)` floor also matches: at max_hp 1 C# heals 1 and the sim heals max(1, 0) = 1. The 1-HP discrepancy G1 records comes from the STARTING HP, not from this expression. Rule 7: src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs are not hashed by this record.
